result:
Sub-issues are in. Type-check is clean and the existing suite passes (617 tests), but I wrote no new tests, so the new behaviour is untested. I also didn't change any visible test.

- **Same-parent no-op:** setting an issue's parent to the one it already has returns the issue unchanged and emits no `issue.updated` event. The spec didn't say either way, so say if you want the event.
- **Notice for a cascade archive:** archiving an open issue notifies its direct parent's assignee if nothing open is left below that parent. Issues archived along with it only have archived parents, so they trigger nothing.
- **Notices skip the event bus:** `notifyIfCompleted` in `src/server/services/issue-service.ts` calls `notify` directly rather than going through an event. That still applies the recipient's preferences and skips the actor.
- **Reads load the whole project:** the roll-up, listing, depth and cycle checks load every issue of the project (new `listAllProjectIssues` in the issue repository) and walk the tree in memory. That avoids any row limit but costs one full-project read per call.

The new service functions are `setIssueParent`, `listSubIssues` and `getIssueRollup`. `createIssue`, `archiveIssue` and `changeIssueStatus` now apply the parent, cascade and completion-notice rules. `IssueHierarchyError` is in `src/lib/issue-hierarchy.ts` and is mapped in `src/lib/errors.ts`. `MAX_SUB_ISSUE_DEPTH`, `IssueRollup` and `setIssueParentSchema` are added as specified.

`sub_issues_completed` is added to the notification kind type, the zod schema, the DB schema enum and the label map in the preferences form. I didn't add a migration; `migrate.ts` stores `kind` as plain text.
